eyebrow: SQL Dialects: T-SQL, PL/SQL, MySQL & Beyond · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 19 · Querying Basics Compared

code:
-- T-SQL: SUBSTRING-only
SELECT SUBSTRING('LTV Academy', 1, 3);  -- 'LTV'

-- Oracle: SUBSTR-only
SELECT SUBSTR('LTV Academy', 1, 3) FROM DUAL;

-- MySQL & PostgreSQL accept BOTH spellings
caption: T-SQL has one name, Oracle has the other — MySQL/Postgres accept both.

eyebrow: Length: LEN vs. LENGTH vs. CHAR_LENGTH
code:
SELECT LEN('LTV Academy');          -- T-SQL
SELECT LENGTH('LTV Academy');       -- Oracle / PostgreSQL
SELECT CHAR_LENGTH('LTV Academy');  -- MySQL (characters, not bytes)
caption: MySQL's LENGTH counts bytes; CHAR_LENGTH counts characters.

code:
SELECT CHARINDEX('Academy', 'LTV Academy');  -- T-SQL: sub first
SELECT INSTR('LTV Academy', 'Academy');      -- Oracle: string first
SELECT LOCATE('Academy', 'LTV Academy');     -- MySQL: sub first
SELECT POSITION('Academy' IN 'LTV Academy'); -- PostgreSQL
caption: CHARINDEX and INSTR reverse each other's argument order — a real bug source.
TRIM, LTRIM, and RTRIM finally give you a break from divergence.
